resources.string: Trail %1$d / 2000 pts · white line = dead-reckoning path · gold cross = start · triangle = current position
The arrow points toward the start; bearing is referenced to magnetic north, and the nose direction is referenced to the top of the phone
Waiting for the first step — the step sensor only reports during real walking

The 0.75m default is only an adult average. Walk 10 natural steps on a known 10m line, divide 10 by the step count, then calibrate; changes only affect future steps and never rewrite the existing trail.
Distance = sum of step count × step length at the time (estimated); distance to start = straight-line distance from the dead-reckoned position to (0,0), not a GPS measurement
No step sensor on this device (TYPE_STEP_COUNTER / TYPE_STEP_DETECTOR) — step reckoning unavailable
Android 10+ requires the \"Physical activity\" permission to read the step counter; it is not granted — grant it and re-enter this page
No rotation-vector sensor on this device — heading unavailable, the trail cannot be computed

Dead reckoning (PDR) depends only on step count and heading, so error accumulates with distance: a hundred-metre route typically drifts 5-10%; turns, hand sway and pocket swing amplify it significantly.
It is only valuable indoors or underground where GPS / stable cell positioning is unavailable; in open terrain, trust satellite positioning.

The 0.75m default is only an adult average; height and gait vary widely — self-calibrate over a known distance. All readouts on this page come from the hardware step counter and rotation-vector sensor; when a sensor is missing or permission is denied, the UI shows \"unavailable\" and never fabricates data.
